population.definition: Population Estimation Survey 2014 result for Banaadir region (which covers the Mogadishu urban area), tabulated by citypopulation.de for Mogadishu. Not a census: Somalia's last published census was 1975 (UNFPA). Includes displaced people according to secondary sources not read here. Press in Nov 2025 (AFP) says about three million inhabitants.

source.title: Somalia: Regions and Cities (Banadir / Muqdisho)
source.publisher: citypopulation.de (cites UNFPA / UN World Urbanization Prospects 2014)
source.quote: For Mogadishu the result of the population estimation survey 2014 for Banaardir is tabulated.

facts.claim: Mogadishu was a major medieval commercial centre on the East African coast, and the Arab traveller Ibn Battuta described it around 1331 as a large town.

source.title: A complete history of Mogadishu (ca. 1100-1892)
source.publisher: African History Extra (Substack), Journal of African Cities chapter 16
source.author: isaac Samuel
source.quote: Ibn Battuta who visited the city around 1331 and described it as "a large town."

facts.claim: The city became a regional gold-trade centre and seaport handling goods from Africa, India and Arab lands.

source.title: Mogadishu, Somalia
source.author: Lee, M.
source.quote: the major center for the gold trade in the region

facts.claim: After Italian occupation in the late 19th century, Mogadishu became the capital of Italian Somaliland; the former colony became independent in 1960.

source.title: Mogadishu, Somalia
source.author: Lee, M.
source.quote: in 1960, the former colony became a fully independent nation known as the United Republic of Somalia

facts.claim: A civil war that began in 1991 devastated the city, which has since been in a long process of revitalisation.

source.title: Mogadishu, Somalia
source.author: Lee, M.
source.quote: has been in a lengthy process of revitalization

facts.claim: In November 2025, AFP reported a building boom in the capital, with the government saying insurgent attacks in Mogadishu fell 86 percent from 2023 to mid-2025 (government claim).

source.title: Rising from the ashes of war: Mogadishu's building boom
source.author: AFP
source.quote: For the first time in decades, the three million inhabitants of the capital Mogadishu are witnessing a building boom

facts.claim: Al Jazeera reported on 25 Nov 2025 that the city is bustling but still on guard against al-Shabab.

source.title: Video: Securing Somalia's capital against al-Shabab threat

places.name: Hamar Weyne (Xamar Weyne) old district, with Fakhr ad-Din and Arba'a Rukun mosques
places.what: Hamar Weyne is one of the two old quarters of Mogadishu, the other being Shangani. It holds medieval mosques including Fakhr ad-Din.

facts.label: Old city
facts.value: Two sections, Shangani and Hamar-Weyne; Shangani thought older

source.title: A complete history of Mogadishu (ca. 1100-1892)
source.author: isaac Samuel
source.quote: The old city consists of two distinct sections known locally as Shangani and Hamar-Weyne

facts.label: Fakhr ad-Din mosque age
facts.value: Built no later than 1269; among Somalia's most significant medieval monuments

source.title: Reviving Somalia's vanishing past: Mogadishu's sacred heritage
source.author: Sagal-Louise Haider
source.quote: Built no later than 1269, it remains one of Somalia's most significant medieval monuments.

places.name: Bakaara Market
places.what: Bakaara (also spelled Bakara or Bakhara) is Mogadishu's major marketplace, in the Hawlwadag district. It grew from a residential area into a commercial hub.

source.title: Community policing in Mogadishu: a case study of Bakhara Market
source.author: Mohamed Ahmed Jama
source.quote: Bakhara Market occupies two square kilometres in the Hawlwadag district of Mogadishu.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: Formerly residential, later a business hub

source.title: Community policing in Mogadishu: a case study of Bakhara Market
source.author: Mohamed Ahmed Jama
source.quote: Formerly a residential neighbourhood, for the last two decades it has been a business hub

source.title: Community policing in Mogadishu: a case study of Bakhara Market
source.author: Mohamed Ahmed Jama
source.quote: It hosts financial institutions, telecommunications companies, import/export firms, media companies, manufacturers

places.name: Somali National Museum
places.what: The National Museum was established in 1933 and closed at the start of the civil war in 1991. After rehabilitation it was reopened on 1 July 2020.

source.title: UNESCO Heritage Emergency Fund supports revival of the Somalia National Museum
source.quote: The National Museum of Somalia was established in 1933

source.title: UNESCO Heritage Emergency Fund supports revival of the Somalia National Museum
source.quote: its national collections were looted, and its staff members dispersed during 30 years of armed conflict.

places.name: Somali National Theatre
places.what: An open-air theatre described by press as Chinese-built. It closed in the early 1990s and has reopened for concerts since 2012.

facts.label: Builder
facts.value: Described as Chinese-built (opening year 1967 not confirmed in a read source)

source.title: Somalia's national theater re-opens its doors after 20 years
source.author: TRTalia Ralph
source.quote: open-air Chinese-built theater

facts.label: Closure
facts.value: Closed in early 1990s with civil war

source.title: Somalia's national theater re-opens its doors after 20 years
source.author: TRTalia Ralph
source.quote: which closed in the early 1990s when the country descended into civil war

source.title: Somali National Theatre Reopens After 20 Years
source.quote: Hundreds of people gathered at the Somali National Theatre for the first concert since it was shut down 20 years ago.

facts.label: 2020 refurbishment
facts.value: Reopened June 2020, funded by businesses, chamber of commerce and civilian workers

source.title: 'Lights up': Somalia's refurbished national theater reopens in Mogadishu
source.quote: the refurbishment was funded by some businesses, the chamber of commerce and contributions by civilian workers.

places.name: Mogadishu Cathedral (ruins)
places.what: An Italian colonial-era cathedral completed in 1928, now a roofless ruin. Its future is debated by Somalis; handle with care as a colonial-era and war-damaged site.

facts.label: Built
facts.value: 1925-1928, modelled on Cefalu Cathedral, Sicily; consecrated 1 March 1928

source.title: Transforming Cefalu in Mogadishu: The Arabo-Normanna Cathedral of Italian Somalia and the Facade of Peaceful Conquest
source.publisher: Journal of the Society of Architectural Historians (abstract via CiteDrive)
source.author: Claire Dillon
source.quote: The Cathedral of Mogadishu now stands in ruins as a shell of Italian colonial ambition in Somalia.

facts.label: Ruin
facts.value: Broken walls and roofless nave symbolise civil-war devastation

source.title: The rubble of empire
source.author: Claire Dillon (interview)
source.quote: Its broken walls and roofless nave have become visual shorthand for the devastation of civil war.

facts.label: Future
facts.value: Debate on reuse; local perspectives needed

source.title: The rubble of empire
source.author: Claire Dillon (interview)
source.quote: Any meaningful future for the site must take local perspectives into account, even if consensus is difficult to achieve.
